name: Card
summary: Groups related content and actions about a single subject.
description: A container that gathers everything about one subject — a person, a product, a project — so it reads as a single unit in a list or a grid. Give each card one clear main action; a card with several competing actions stops being one unit.
whenToUse: Several pieces of information belong to one subject and should be scanned together.
The page shows a list or grid of comparable items.
whenNotToUse: You need page-level layout structure. Use the page's own layout instead.
The content is a plain run of text with nothing to group. Leave it ungrouped.

variant.default: The everyday choice, separated from the page by a thin edge.
variant.elevated: Lifts off the page, for a card that sits above other content or needs emphasis.

dos: Keep one main call-to-action per card.
donts: Don't nest cards more than one level deep.
Don't make the card and a button inside it separately clickable.

notes: A card is just a container with no meaning of its own. Add a role and a name only when it is a landmark region or is itself clickable.
If the whole card is clickable, give it an accessible name and make it reachable by keyboard.
Don't let the lift be the only thing carrying meaning; anyone who can't see it needs the same information in words.
